channel.title: Longhand | The Dry Text Co.
channel.description: Writing about writing, from a content agency in Ahmedabad. A new piece most mornings.

item.title: Brochures: does anyone read them, and what to put in the one they do
item.description: Most brochures go in a drawer. The one that gets read is read by someone who wasn't in the meeting.

item.title: Should your website show prices?
item.description: Price on request feels safe and reads as expensive. When to show the number, and how to write it.

item.title: Writing a price increase message customers don't leave over
item.description: Most price increase messages apologise for a paragraph and hide the number. Put the number first.

item.title: Writing a case study when the client won't let you name them
item.description: The client said no to the logo, so the case study never got written. How to write one that works without a name.

item.title: How to write a job post that good people answer
item.description: Most job posts read like a notice, so the good people scroll past. What to write instead.

item.title: The Contact page: the last page before money, and the least written
item.description: The page where a visitor decides to spend money is usually a form and a map. What to write there instead.

item.title: Why every Diwali post looks the same, and how to write one that doesn't
item.description: Diya, rangoli, prosperity in gold. How to write the Diwali post only your business could send.

item.title: Writing a hoarding: seven words at sixty kilometres an hour
item.description: A hoarding gets one glance from someone driving at sixty. Seven words is plenty. Here is what to cut.

item.title: Email subject lines that get opened without lying
item.description: Fake Re:, false Urgent, a quick question that isn't. How to get the open without the small lie.

item.title: How many revisions a writer should include, and what counts as one
item.description: Two rounds of revisions means nothing until someone says what a round is. How to agree on one.

item.title: Writing a product description for an Indian D2C brand
item.description: Most product pages say premium quality and stop. How to answer the doubts a photo can't.

item.title: Exclamation marks, and other ways copy sounds nervous
item.description: Exclamation marks, apologies and hedges make a business sound unsure. How to spot them, and a ten-minute fix.

item.title: Company page or founder profile: where a B2B brand should post
item.description: A company page and a founder's profile do different jobs. What each is for, and who should post what.

item.title: Writing an FAQ page from the questions people actually ask
item.description: Most FAQ pages answer questions nobody asked. Where the real ones are, and how to answer them in one line.

item.title: Hinglish in brand copy: when it works and when it's a costume
item.description: Hinglish works when it is how your customer talks, and reads like a costume when it isn't. Three tests.

item.title: Do you need a tagline?
item.description: The line people ask for first and need last. When a tagline earns its place, and what to write before it.

item.title: The cold mail first line: what to write before they delete
item.description: The first line shows in the inbox before anyone opens the mail. What it has to do, and what wastes it.

item.title: How to ask a customer for a testimonial you can actually use
item.description: Most testimonials persuade nobody. The four questions to ask a customer instead, and when.

item.title: The paragraph on your Google listing, and how to write it
item.description: The paragraph on your Google listing, read by people about to call. What to put in it, and what to leave out.

item.title: How long an Instagram caption should be
item.description: Instagram shows a line or two, then hides the rest. How long a caption should be, post by post.

item.title: How to give feedback on a draft, so round two is the last
item.description: Most second drafts miss because the feedback described a feeling, not a fix. What to write in the margin instead.

item.title: Copywriter or content writer: which one you actually need
item.description: Used as if they were one job. What each one is for, and how to tell which your project needs.

item.title: How to write a WhatsApp broadcast people don't mute
item.description: It arrives between the family group and the school group. The preview line, the shape, and how often is too often.

item.title: Your homepage headline has one job
item.description: A stranger gives it about three seconds. What it has to answer, and the five kinds that fail.

item.title: Nine words that make every Indian brand sound the same
item.description: Seamless, curated, bespoke, passionate, and one whole sentence shape. Why they're there, and what to write instead.
